edition.notes: The act is printed in Italian under the rubric Acta Congregationum; no Latin version appears in the gazette. Signed by Cardinal Leonardo Sandri, Prefect.

passages.context: The three dispositions approved by Pope Francis on 23 December 2013: the faculty conferred on Eastern Hierarchs in circumscriptions outside the traditional territories, with a duty to inform the local Latin bishop in writing before ordaining a married candidate; the faculty conferred on Ordinaries for Eastern faithful lacking a proper Hierarch; and the reservation of the faculty to the Congregation where Eastern faithful have no specific administrative structure.

passages.context: The introductory note: c. 758 par. 3 CCEO as the governing canon; the statement that at present all the Eastern Catholic Churches may admit married men to the diaconate and presbyterate except the Syro-Malabar and Syro-Malankara Churches; the 1890 Propaganda Fide prohibition, the 1913 Canadian decree, and the decrees Cum data fuerit (1929), Qua sollerti (1929), and Graeci-Rutheni (1930) with their own Acta citations; the estimate of some 200,000 Ruthenian faithful passing to Orthodoxy; and the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith's decision of 20 February 2008 approved by Benedict XVI.

work.author: Congregation for the Eastern Churches
work.description: The act of the Congregation for the Eastern Churches, dated 14 June 2014 and approved by Pope Francis in an audience of 23 December 2013, conferring on Eastern Hierarchs and Ordinaries outside the traditional Eastern territories the faculty to permit the pastoral service of married Eastern clergy and to ordain married candidates, while reserving the faculty to the dicastery where Eastern faithful have no proper structure. Its introductory note surveys the restrictions imposed from 1890 onward and states that all the Eastern Catholic Churches except the Syro-Malabar and Syro-Malankara may admit married men to the diaconate and presbyterate.
work.title: Pontificia Praecepta de clero uxorato orientali
